title: Interview tip: sell the value, not just the project
oneliner: Don't just describe the AI project you built - state the value you will bring to their organization if hired, even if the interviewer never asks.
says: In AI solution architect or enterprise AI architect interviews, do not only talk about the AI agent or GenAI project you implemented. Talk about the value you will bring to their organization if hired. Some interviewers still use the legacy style and never ask about value - then it is your responsibility to say it anyway. Do not talk about the project only; connect it to the value you would bring them.
explained: The distinction is past versus future tense. Project talk proves capability; value talk proves relevance. The interviewer is buying your next three years, not your last project - so the winning move is translation: 'I built X, which cut Y by Z% - and looking at your environment, the same approach applies to your A and B.' That is the company research from his interview-prep reels surfacing at the answer level.

His point about legacy interviewers is practical: many panels never ask the value question, and candidates leave having never made their actual case. Volunteering it - politely, at the summary moment of an answer - changes what they remember about you when the debrief happens.
takeaway: Every project answer should land on their business: 'and here is where that maps to your world.' Say it even when unasked.
